transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Torres (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (Windsor Head of ML), Priya Rao (Windsor CTO), David Li (Infra), Rachel Kim (Security), Owen Park (Data Eng)

Summary (auto-generated): Windsor is running a production recommender + customer chat pipeline and is exploring Redwood Dedicated to get reserved GPUs and network isolation. Key asks: predictable throughput for peak trading hours, burst strategy into Hosted for spikes, SOC2/KMS details, RBAC/SSO integration, and a benchmark to validate latency and cost.

Transcript:
00:00 Samir Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll just do quick intros and then jump into your workload and constraints ok
00:08 Mark Chen: yeah thanks, um Mark here, head of ML at Windsor. we've got a couple people from infra and security on the line too
00:14 Priya Rao: Priya, CTO — we'll be evaluating from product/ops perspective, timeline is Q2 pilot if possible
00:21 David Li: David, infra, mostly network and ops questions from me
00:25 Rachel Kim: Rachel, security. we'll want SOC2 docs, encryption, KMS, logs, that sort of thing
00:31 Samir Patel: awesome. elena and i from Redwood, elena is our solutions engineer, she'll dig into perf and sizing
00:36 Elena Torres: hi all, glad to be here. quick quick agenda: current infra + workloads, expected peak QPS and latency targets, security/compliance, and then sizing + burst strategy
00:48 Mark Chen: cool. quick background: we run a recommender that handles near-real-time scoring plus a customer-facing chat assistant for support. combined, about 30m tokens/day today but spikes to 3k qps for short windows during mornings and product launches
01:05 Owen Park: adding — a lot of requests are short context, 64–512 tokens, but we also have some long sessions up to 2k tokens for support transcripts
01:15 Elena Torres: ok good. what's your 95th percentile latency target for the recommender and chat?
01:21 Mark Chen: recommender needs ~200–300 ms 95p for the short calls; chat can tolerate up to 800–1,200 ms for complex threads. cost is also critical — we can't blow out inference spend with spikes
01:36 Samir Patel: totally — that's where Dedicated helps with predictable throughput. just to align terminology: Dedicated = reserved GPU pools with isolation, Hosted = our public multi-tenant API, Private = VPC/on-prem managed by the customer. Does that match your mental model?
01:49 Priya Rao: yes. we're leaning Dedicated because we want reserved capacity and data isolation, but we also want burst to Hosted for occasional spikes to avoid huge commits
01:58 David Li: plus we want the network kept inside our VPC and keys in our KMS — no plaintext keys in a hosted environment if possible
02:07 Rachel Kim: and audit logs, SSO via SAML, RBAC controls for teams. do you support SCIM for user provisioning?
02:15 Samir Patel: yes — we support SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC roles, and can integrate with major IdPs. for KMS we have integrations and options: customer-managed KMS in the Private option; for Dedicated we do offer CMK passthrough in many regions, we'll share the exact list in the security pack
02:33 Mark Chen: great. from perf side, how do you do autoscaling for Dedicated? we don't want to overcommit but need to ensure latency at spikes
02:42 Elena Torres: good question. Dedicated pools are reserved but you can configure burst policies. typical pattern: reserve baseline capacity sized for expected steady-state QPS, and allow configured burst to Hosted or to an elastic pool if you have reserved burst capacity. burst is governed by policy — e.g., priority routing by latency SLO, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants if capacity exhausted
03:04 Mark Chen: when you say "burst to Hosted" what happens to data — is it still isolated? concerns from security
03:11 Samir Patel: important to call out — when you burst to Hosted, you can choose to redact sensitive fields or route only non-sensitive traffic. We can also enforce VPC egress rules and use TLS + customer KMS for logs. If you need zero egress, then that points to Private or on-prem
03:28 Rachel Kim: ok we have a requirement that PII never leaves our VPC for certain tenants. so for those, we need guaranteed on-prem or fully private deployment
03:36 Elena Torres: understood. you can mix: Dedicated for most workloads and Private for regulated tenants. The routing policy can tag requests and route accordingly
03:48 Owen Park: question on GPU types — what hardware do Dedicated pools run on? we use a mix of fp16/quantized models, curious about supported cards and quantization paths
03:57 Elena Torres: Dedicated supports A100 and H100 families depending on region, plus we have support for 4-bit/8-bit quantized paths on our runtime. kernel selection and sequence-length optimizations happen at runtime — we'll profile your workload during the benchmark to pick best kernels and quant configs
04:19 David Li: and how about KV cache and prefix caching — we have a lot of repeated prompts so caching could save a lot of cost
04:26 Elena Torres: yes we have prefix and KV caching, configurable TTLs and per-route caching. that can dramatically reduce token compute for repeated content. we'll want your prompt traces to tune cache keys
04:36 Mark Chen: ok good. can you explain how billing would work for Dedicated plus burst? like, committed vs burst usage?
04:43 Samir Patel: billing: you pay for reserved capacity (monthly commit) and usage. Burst to Hosted is billed at Hosted rates for the burst portion; committed reserved capacity gets a lower unit rate. We also provide cost analytics per token and per-route, so you can see where burst is impacting unit economics
05:03 Priya Rao: timeline — if we want to pilot in Q2, what does onboarding look like and how long to spin up a Dedicated pool?
05:10 Elena Torres: typical provisioning is 2–4 weeks once contract signed for a Dedicated pool in a supported region; shorter if we have pre-warmed inventory. onboarding includes network setup (VPC peering or private link), config, and a benchmarking run
 n05:30 Mark Chen: small transcription typo there, but ok — for the benchmarking run, we want to validate 95p latency and cost per 1k tokens. can you run a sample run with our traces?
05:39 Elena Torres: yes — we request sample traces, typical traffic generator script, and we'll run a 48-hour soak + spike tests. we'll capture p50/p95/p99, kps, GPU utilization, and cost breakdown. we can run both on Dedicated pool and a burst path to Hosted to compare
06:00 David Li: network question — do you support VPC endpoints/private link? we need to avoid open internet egress for Dedicated
06:08 Samir Patel: yes we support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and can provision customer-facing endpoints with strict IP allowlists. we'll detail network diagrams in the security pack
06:18 Rachel Kim: about logs — how long do you retain audit logs and can we push logs to our SIEM?
06:24 Samir Patel: we can stream audit logs to your SIEM, and retention options are configurable. default retention in Dedicated can be increased for enterprise customers; we'll include options in the security doc
06:35 Mark Chen: tradeoff question — we're nervous about under-committing and paying for too much. any guidance on sizing for variable daily peaks and holiday surges?
06:43 Elena Torres: we usually recommend baseline sizing for expected 95p steady-state and reserve additional capacity for economy-of-scale. for big unpredictable spikes we propose a hybrid: baseline Dedicated sized to cover typical peaks + burst policy to Hosted for <5-10% of peak minutes. we also support scheduled scaling windows for known events (deployments, product launches) so you can temporarily increase reserved pools for those dates
07:10 Priya Rao: can you guarantee latency SLOs if we burst to Hosted?
07:14 Samir Patel: guarantees differ — Dedicated pools have SLA-backed latency/uptime targets. Burst to Hosted is best-effort and we provide latency estimates and fallback policies; if you require tight SLOs for all traffic, Private or larger Dedicated commitments are the way to go
07:28 Owen Park: what's the minimum commitment size? we are medium-sized, not huge — curious about minimums and pricing tiers
07:34 Samir Patel: minimum varies by region; we have starter Dedicated configs (small pool of 2–4 GPUs) for mid-market customers. pricing sheet will show tiered discounts for larger commits. we'll send that after call
07:44 David Li: encryption at rest — do you support customer-managed keys for Dedicated logs and model artifacts?
07:49 Samir Patel: yes, we support CMKs. For model artifacts we can use customer KMS in Private; for Dedicated we can do envelope encryption with CMK passthrough in many regions — again, details in pack
07:59 Mark Chen: operational question — how do rollouts and model versioning work? we need canary and A/B rollouts for new model versions
08:07 Elena Torres: Redwood Console supports per-route rollouts, canary %, A/B, and automatic fallback if quality/regression alerts fire. we can tie rollouts to eval sets and monitor quality metrics during rollout with automatic rollback policies
08:27 Rachel Kim: regulatory question — data residency: some EU customers require that inference never leaves EU zones. can you pin Dedicated pools to regions?
08:35 Samir Patel: yes, Dedicated can be regionally pinned. for strict residency we recommend Private in your EU region or Dedicated pools provisioned in the EU with VPC routing
08:44 Mark Chen: ok. one more on models — we run both open-source models and licensed third-party ones. can you host custom models in Dedicated?
08:52 Elena Torres: yes, you can bring your own model (BYOM) — we support model packaging and version pinning. we'll want to validate license terms for third-party models and ensure runtime compatibility; we'll note any kernel/quant requirements in the onboarding checklist
09:08 Owen Park: question about metrics — do you provide per-token cost breakdown and token-level tracing? we need to attribute cost by route and team
09:15 Samir Patel: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route breakdowns, attribution to teams, and tracing hooks you can integrate with your observability stack
09:24 Mark Chen: walk me through the benchmark itself — what's a typical deliverable?
09:28 Elena Torres: deliverables: benchmark report with latency histograms, GPU utilization, model configs used, quantization options tested, cost-per-1k tokens for resident vs burst, and recommended Dedicated pool sizing + cache config. we'll also include a runbook for scaling and suggested routing policies
09:46 David Li: who will we coordinate with on our side for the benchmark? Owen and Mark will provide traces; Rachel will sign off on any data handling
09:53 Mark Chen: yes we'll share sanitized traces; Rachel will confirm PII redaction approach
09:58 Samir Patel: perfect. quick callouts: for the benchmark we'll need a signed NDA and SOW to provision Dedicated. timeline: if we get docs this week we can start a perf run next week.
10:15 Priya Rao: ok, commercial question — if we commit to a 12-month Dedicated contract, are there migration supports if we want to later move to Private?
10:22 Samir Patel: yes — we support migration paths and can do Private onboarding; depending on contract we can amortize migration effort and offer a technical migration package
10:34 Rachel Kim: last security clarifying Q: do you support hardware-backed HSM for key storage?
10:41 Elena Torres: for Private we can integrate with HSMs; for Dedicated we support KMS integrations and can work with partners for HSM-backed keys in select regions
10:55 Mark Chen: ok let's recap next steps
11:00 Samir Patel: recap: Samir to send pricing + sizing sheet and draft SOW/NDA; Elena to provision benchmark infra and test harness once we have traces; Windsor to provide traces and security checklist; schedule follow-up technical deep-dive next week to review benchmark plan. sound right?
11:18 Priya Rao: yes that works. target pilot start mid-April if everything goes smooth
11:24 Rachel Kim: I'll send security checklist by Thursday.
11:28 Owen Park: I'll work with Elena on traces, expect them by Friday
11:32 Samir Patel: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites and links to the security docs
11:38 Mark Chen: thanks all.
11:40 Samir Patel: bye

Notes on transcript quality: some timestamps approximate; occasional ASR mis-hear (n05:30 tag) and transcription artifacts. PII redaction discussed — Windsor will provide sanitized traces for bench.
